additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).

subtypes.Fasting: Intentionally stopping food intake for a certain period to prevent weight gain.
subtypes.Excessive Exercise: Repetitively performing exercise at a level that exceeds physical limits to prevent weight gain.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating accompanied by a sense of loss of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, fasting, overexercise, or misuse of medications to prevent weight gain. Self-evaluation is typically unduly influenced by body weight and shape, and individuals often oscillate between restrictive dieting and episodes of overeating. The course can be chronic or intermittent, with symptoms waxing and waning in response to stress, transitions, and changes in interpersonal or work demands. It is distinguished from binge-eating disorder by the presence of regular compensatory behaviors and from anorexia nervosa, binge-purge type, by the absence of significantly low body weight.

patient.stressor: Martin’s firm began encouraging senior managers to plan gradual retirement, and about five months ago he shifted to a reduced schedule with the understanding that he would fully retire within two years. The loss of daily structure and the sudden extra time at home, combined with his long-standing tendency to get absorbed in creative projects, led him to alternate between periods of skipping proper meals while painting or working on models and then eating large, improvised meals late in the evening. Over four months, he responded to these episodes by imposing rigid rules on himself—like long, compensatory exercise walks and strict next-day restrictions—which only made his eating feel more out of control when he inevitably broke those rules. He came to psychiatric care after his primary doctor, noticing weight fluctuations and hearing about his increasingly extreme cycles of "making up" for what he ate, urged him to talk with a mental health professional before the pattern worsened as he approached full retirement.
patient.chief_complaint: “I keep swinging between eating way too much and then trying to ‘make up for it’ with these harsh rules and routines, and it’s starting to take over my days.”

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: Even on days when my wife tells me I look fine, I stand in front of the bathroom mirror pinching at my stomach and thinking, ‘you’re getting soft and useless,’ and that thought pretty much decides whether I feel like I had a good day or a bad one, no matter what else I did.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).
S047.manifestation: After one of those big late-night meals, I’ll force myself to do these long, almost punishing walks the next day and stick to coffee and maybe an apple, telling myself I don’t deserve a real meal until I’ve ‘balanced the books,’ even if I’m tired and hungry.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: When my wife goes to bed and the house is quiet, I’ll end up in the kitchen picking at leftovers, then bread, then cheese and cereal and whatever else is in reach until I’ve eaten enough for two or three dinners without really noticing until I see all the dirty dishes.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start in on that kind of eating, it feels like something clicks off in my brain—I'll tell myself, 'you should stop now,' but my hands just keep reaching for more food like I’m on autopilot and I only snap out of it when I’m uncomfortably full.
